# SimVLA 1.0.0 — release draft

SimVLA provides kitchen generation, skill composition and simulation-data tools
for mobile manipulation. This release includes the CPU package and simulator
source interfaces; the paper's training pipeline is not included.

## Start here

The CPU quickstart creates a kitchen, task, and reproducibility manifest without Isaac Sim. The
package also supports task and skill inspection, goal validation, and SimVQA conversion. Follow
the [installation guide](https://github.com/kyounginbaik/SimVLA/blob/v1.0.0/docs/installation.md)
and the ordered workflows in the README.

Simulator sources support kitchen and goal generation, SimAction/SimVQA collection, and
recorded-action evaluation with external runtime dependencies and assets. Kitchen-813,
seed-0 reference collection, LeRobot export, physical replay, and SimVQA validation
have historical passes for all three robots. Anubis and AI Worker replay use recorded joint motor targets
plus base-pose feedback. This is bounded local reproduction, not arbitrary-task
reliability or an external independent reproduction; use the exact documented profiles.
Fresh public-runtime chains now have bounded passes for all three robots. AI
Worker's kitchen-813 loaded-home and repaired-basin chain uses the named physics-12
profile and a documented hybrid replay mode; it does not establish multi-seed or
arbitrary-scene reliability.

## Validation

- Fresh CPU installation, scene/task generation, example VQA conversion, and portable
  regression tests pass locally. Current counts and commands are in release validation.
- Dataset-integrity tests check real Parquet/video fixtures, finite values, indices,
  timestamps, dimensions, FPS, and decoded frame counts.
- Separate simulator/export environments pass dependency checks. The isolated
  simulator passes three-robot RTX 3090 camera/physics smokes, and a fresh locked
  CPU exporter passes frame-aligned synthetic exports for all three robot schemas.
- Fresh public Anubis collection/replay (2426755 → 2429275) produced 1,212
  frames and 275 QA examples. Fresh RBY1 (2424756 → 2426057), with approved
  camera-07 mounts, produced 1,155 frames and 164 QA examples.
- AI Worker native-BoDex extended carry has an earlier passing reference
  (2408283 → 2412231). Later loaded-home/repaired-basin collection 2437904 and
  independent replay 2437908 passed on the documented physics-12 profile, with
  SimVQA validation. The older failures remain recorded and are not treated as
  passes for this newer control mode.
- Wheel/source-distribution scope checks and runtime provenance tooling are included.
  Hosted CI and release artifacts must be verified at publication; local evidence is not
  a hosted CI result.

## Scope

Complete simulator use still requires the documented external robot and kitchen
assets. Neither GPU smokes nor bounded reference tasks establish arbitrary-task
reliability, trained-policy performance, or paper-result reproduction. See
[release validation](https://github.com/kyounginbaik/SimVLA/blob/v1.0.0/docs/validation.md) and the
[reproducibility map](https://github.com/kyounginbaik/SimVLA/blob/v1.0.0/docs/reproducibility.md)
before comparing results.
